method: Claude built a new generator family, circle_steps (folder round-and-round, shown as Round and Round), for the 'going round in circles' concepts, which had no family: SEQUENCES_CYCLIC, MODULAR_ARITHMETIC and CYCLE_DETECTION. It draws on four tasks from the map (Drawing Stars, Hangar Carousel, Cipher 8 and Tortoise and Hare) under an original fun-fair story with our own wording and pictures. Level 1 counts a counter round a ring-shaped game board past the last square; level 2 reads the step of a finished string-art star (the Drawing Stars idea); level 3 asks how many pins a loop of every k-th pin touches, which is n / gcd(n, k); level 4 counts the fewest presses to bring Ferris wheel cars to the platform in a set order, the shorter way round and measured from where the wheel is now (the circular distance of Hangar Carousel and the relative counting of Cipher 8, asked as a best case rather than the source's worst case); level 5 moves a slow and a fast go-kart along a straight road into a loop and asks where they first meet (the Tortoise and Hare idea). All answers are typed, and every wrong value a habit gives is tagged. Every problem passes check_circle_steps.py, which rebuilds the problem from the picture, puts the spots in clockwise order by their angle in the drawing, and solves it again by stepping one place at a time (turning a list of cars both ways, following the track's arrows for both karts) instead of using modular arithmetic; it also checks every line of the explanation. All 2097 corrupted answers, tags, explanations and pictures in the mutation trials are caught. Two findings from building it. First, the 'every pin' habit gives the right count whenever n and k share no factor, so level 3 only uses pairs that share one; the answer is then always smaller than n, which the explanation's written-out loop makes plain rather than leaving it as a pattern to spot. Second, on the kart track the slow and fast karts close the gap by exactly one square a second once both are on the loop, so they can never jump past each other and the first meeting is always a shared square, at the first whole number of laps that is at least the length of the road. The Bracelet idea (matching a ring under rotation and reflection) is not built here; it is listed as a candidate together with a trees candidate, the next largest group of concepts with no family.

ladder.question: step
ladder.note: Count round the board one square at a time. After the last square comes square 1 again.

ladder.question: label
ladder.note: Follow one line from pin 1 and count the steps round to its other end, the short way.

ladder.question: visits
ladder.note: Keep jumping k pins until you land on pin 1 again. The loop can come back before it has been everywhere.

ladder.question: turns
ladder.note: Each move starts from where the wheel is now. Count both ways round and take the shorter one.

ladder.question: meet
ladder.note: Move both karts one second at a time and write down their squares until they share one.

generator_candidates.why: Stepping round a circle had no family. A counter round a ring board, string-art stars (read the step; count the pins one loop touches, n / gcd), a Ferris wheel (shortest way round, from where it is now) and two karts on a road into a loop (where they first meet); every answer typed and checked by stepping one place at a time.

Matching a ring under rotation and reflection (SEQUENCES_CYCLIC) is the one idea in the circles group that circle_steps does not ask. A string of beads and four rings; the wrong rings come from an adjacent swap, reading one way only, or matching only from the first bead. Could become a level 1 below circle_steps' counting or a family of its own.

Trees (TREE, BST, SCHEMA) are the largest group of concepts with no family, across Beaver Dam, Binary Hotel, Beaver Lunch and Super Power Family. Placing keys in a search tree, following left and right to find one, and counting levels; distractors from going the wrong way at a node, comparing with the root only, and counting nodes instead of levels.

misconceptions.description: Treats a circle of numbered spots as a straight line, so a count never goes past the last number back to 1.
misconceptions.remediation: Point to the last number on the circle. What comes after it? Keep counting from there.

misconceptions.description: Counts the square the counter starts on as the first step, so it lands one square short.
misconceptions.remediation: The first step takes the counter off its square. Count the squares it lands on, not the one it leaves.

misconceptions.description: Doesn't count the step from the last number back to 1, so it lands one square too far.
misconceptions.remediation: Going from the last square to square 1 is a step like any other. Count it.

misconceptions.description: Counts the pins a line skips over instead of how many places on it goes, one too few.
misconceptions.remediation: Count the steps from the pin where the line starts to the pin where it ends, landing on each pin in between.

misconceptions.description: Counts the pins from one end of a line to the other, both ends included, one too many.
misconceptions.remediation: Put a finger on the start pin and count each move to the next pin. The start pin is not a move.

misconceptions.description: Counts from one end of a line to the other the long way round the circle.
misconceptions.remediation: A line joins two pins. Count the steps between them the short way round.

misconceptions.description: Assumes that joining every k-th pin always reaches every pin, which is only true when k and the number of pins share no factor.
misconceptions.remediation: Follow the lines and write down each pin you land on. Do you come back to 1 before you have been everywhere?

misconceptions.description: Stops when the loop first goes past pin 1, rather than when it lands on pin 1 again.
misconceptions.remediation: The pencil only stops when it lands on pin 1. Going past it doesn't count; keep going round.

misconceptions.description: Counts pin 1 again when the loop gets back to it, so the count is one too many.
misconceptions.remediation: Pin 1 is where the loop begins and ends. Count it once.

misconceptions.description: Always turns the circle the same way, even when the other way is shorter.
misconceptions.remediation: For each move, count both ways round and take the shorter one.

misconceptions.description: Measures every move from where the circle started, not from where it is now.
misconceptions.remediation: After each move the circle stays where it stopped. Measure the next move from there.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a slow and a fast runner meet where the loop begins.
misconceptions.remediation: Move both runners one second at a time and write down where each one is. Stop when they share a square.

misconceptions.description: Thinks the loop leads back to the start of the track, so the runners meet where they began.
misconceptions.remediation: Follow the arrows from the last square of the loop. Where does it lead: back to the start, or round the loop again?
